title: Electrical, solar and overhead services
audience: Trainees and workers on the roof soft washing track, working under supervision, who may see overhead services or solar arrays on a roof. This lesson does not grant any right to work on, isolate or repair solar or electrical installations.
learningOutcomes: Identify overhead services, roof-mounted solar arrays and electrical equipment that change a roof job's risk.
Explain why a solar array's DC cables can remain live when the mains power is switched off.
Apply stop-work and referral rules when a roof has live, damaged or unidentified electrical equipment.

instruction.heading: Overhead services near the roof
instruction.body: Overhead power lines, service drops and communications cables may run close to a roof, its edges and its gutters. A ladder, a pole, a hose or a tool can reach a line by accident, and contact can be fatal. Before work starts, survey the roof perimeter and the path of any equipment for overhead services. Queensland's WorkSafe page sets a 3-metre exclusion zone for overhead powerlines up to 132 kV, including low-voltage lines usually carried on poles (no date shown). The NSW code of practice on work near overhead and underground electric lines (cover dated May 2026, in force from 22 May 2026) sets 3.0 metres for ordinary persons from lines up to 132,000 V. For conductive materials such as roofing and guttering near low-voltage overhead service lines, it sets 4.0 metres. For non-conductive materials it sets 1.5 metres, for hand-held tools 0.5 metres, and for driving or traversing mobile plant 0.6 metres. Where a line is within reach, or its distance cannot be confirmed against these figures, stop and refer the job to the network operator or a qualified person before the equipment is moved.

instruction.heading: Solar arrays on the roof
instruction.body: Many roofs carry photovoltaic arrays. Energy Safe Victoria guidance (reviewed 15 April 2025) says that DC supply cables can remain live after the supply is switched off, and that contact with them should be prevented. The WA government guide adds that the panels keep generating during the day even when the main power has been disconnected (page last updated 26 November 2024). A solar array can also generate electricity while light falls on it, so switching off the mains does not make the array safe. Treat every panel, cable and connector as live, and do not touch them.

instruction.heading: Isolation and who may do it
instruction.body: Energy Safe Victoria's guidance (page reviewed 15 April 2025) says that installing and maintaining PV systems is licensed electrical installation work, and that damaged cables or equipment must be repaired by a licensed electrical installation worker. As a rule for this course, a roof soft washing worker does not test, isolate or repair any solar or electrical system, and refers these to a licensed electrician. The Western Australian guide (last updated 26 November 2024) says DC isolators need to be verified by a licensed electrician. In New South Wales, electrical wiring work, including repairing, needs an electrical licence or certificate (page last updated 23 June 2026). Plain panel washing is not stated by the official pages to need a licence.

instruction.heading: Water and electrical components
instruction.body: Water on connectors, inverters, junction boxes and wiring can cause a fault or a shock. Soft washing involves water and products, so keep the spray away from electrical components, inverters and any junction box, and keep the spray from the electrical side of any equipment. This is a safe-work rule for this course; no official source reviewed in this draft states it as a legal requirement. Where water reaches electrical equipment, stop, and refer the equipment to a licensed electrician before the job continues.

instruction.heading: Recognising a fault and stopping
instruction.body: Stop work and refer when you see or suspect exposed wiring, a damaged cable, a burnt or discoloured connector, a panel that is cracked or hot, a smell of burning, a buzzing or spitting sound, or water near an inverter or junction box. Do not touch the fault. Keep people and animals clear of the area. Record what was seen, where, and when, and tell the site controller and the owner in writing.

instruction.heading: Licence and authority boundary
instruction.body: Licence notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems, electrical installations, inverters or wiring. Victorian guidance treats PV installation and maintenance as licensed electrical installation work, and says damaged cables or equipment must be repaired by a licensed electrical installation worker. In New South Wales, electrical wiring work, including repairing, needs an electrical licence or certificate. Plain panel washing is not stated by the official pages to need a licence. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

procedure: Survey the roof perimeter, gutters and equipment path for overhead lines and service drops before work starts.
Confirm whether a solar array or other electrical equipment is on the roof and record its position.
Keep ladders, poles, hoses and tools clear of overhead lines, and refer any line that is within reach or unclear.
Keep spray away from inverters, junction boxes, connectors and wiring, and do not treat switching off the mains as making the array safe.
Do not touch, move or clean any solar connector, cable or electrical component.
Stop and refer on any sign of exposed wiring, damage, burning, hot components or water near electrical equipment.
Record the observations, the people told and the referral to a licensed electrician or the network operator.
Do not restart the work near the affected equipment until a qualified person has confirmed it is safe to do so.

workedExamples.situation: A roof has a solar array along the north plane, and the owner says the inverter has been switched off for the wash. A service line runs close to the eaves at the rear.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Can the wash go ahead once the inverter is off?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The inverter switch is not treated as making the array safe, because DC cables can remain live and panels can generate while light falls on them (Energy Safe Victoria guidance, reviewed 15 April 2025, and the WA guide, last updated 26 November 2024). The service line also needs a clearance check against the Queensland 3-metre exclusion zone and the NSW code's 4.0-metre distance for metal roofing and guttering near low-voltage service lines. Keep the spray away from the array, do not touch the cables, and refer the electrical isolation to a licensed electrician, because this course does not allow a cleaner to isolate the array. The wash may resume only on the ground-based or excluded parts of the scope.

workedExamples.situation: During the wash, a worker notices a connector on the array has a black, burnt mark, and the spray has reached a junction box.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop the spray, keep it away from the box, and do not touch the connector or the box. Keep people clear, record the mark and the water contact with its location, and tell the owner and the site controller in writing. Refer to a licensed electrician before any further work near the array.

equipmentAndPpe: Overhead line survey checklist for the roof perimeter and equipment path
Photographs of the solar array and its connectors, marked with positions
PPE as specified in the job pack, with no tools or equipment touching live components

commonErrors.error: Assuming a roof array is safe because the inverter is switched off.
commonErrors.prevention: Treat every panel, cable and connector as live, and refer the isolation to a licensed electrician.

commonErrors.error: Moving a ladder or pole near an overhead line without a check.
commonErrors.prevention: Survey the path first and refer any line that is within reach or unclear.

commonErrors.error: Spraying water onto a junction box or inverter.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the spray away from electrical components and stop if water reaches them.

commonErrors.error: Touching a burnt or damaged connector to see what is wrong.
commonErrors.prevention: Do not touch the fault. Record it and refer it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Overhead services: Queensland's WorkSafe page sets a 3 metre exclusion zone for overhead powerlines up to 132 kV, including low-voltage lines (no date shown). The NSW code of practice on work near overhead and underground electric lines (in force from 22 May 2026) sets 3.0 metres for ordinary persons from lines up to 132,000 V, and 4.0 metres for conductive materials such as roofing and guttering near low-voltage overhead service lines. Refer any line that is within reach or whose clearance cannot be confirmed.

Solar DC cables can remain live after the supply is switched off (Energy Safe Victoria guidance, reviewed 15 April 2025). The same guidance says installing and maintaining PV systems is licensed electrical installation work.

Licence notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems, inverters, wiring or electrical installations. Victorian guidance treats PV installation and maintenance as licensed electrical installation work, and says damaged cables or equipment must be repaired by a licensed electrical installation worker. New South Wales treats repairing as part of electrical wiring work, which needs an electrical licence or certificate (electrical page, last updated 23 June 2026). Plain panel washing is not stated by the official pages to need a licence.

qualityStandard: The roof perimeter and equipment path are checked for overhead services before work starts.
Solar arrays and electrical components are identified, and no roof method treats the array as safe without evidence.
Spray is kept away from electrical components, and any water contact is recorded and referred.
No electrical component is touched, moved or repaired by a worker on this course.
documentationEvidence: Overhead services survey record with the clearance decision
Position record for any solar array and electrical component on the roof
Stop and referral record for any fault or water contact, with the person notified
Referral to a licensed electrician or network operator, with the outcome
summary: Overhead lines and solar arrays change the risk of every roof job.

Switching off the mains does not make a solar array safe: Energy Safe Victoria's PV guidance isolates the supply at the main switchboard, says DC cables may stay live, and does not mention the inverter switch.
Keep spray away from electrical components, and stop and refer any fault or water contact.
This lesson grants no right to work on or isolate electrical or solar equipment.

knowledgeChecks.question: A solar array's inverter has been switched off. What does this mean for the roof wash?
options: The array is safe to touch once the inverter is off and the panels are cool
The wash can use any spray pattern on the panels, the frame and the cables
The array no longer needs a check before the wash begins on the roof on the day
The array can still generate and its DC cables can remain live, so it is not safe

knowledgeChecks.question: A service line is within reach of a ladder and its clearance is not known. What is the correct action?
options: Stop, keep the equipment clear, and refer to the network operator or a qualified person
Move the ladder quickly past the line before the next gust of wind arrives
Ask the customer to cover the line with a sheet of heavy plastic for the job
Continue carefully and keep an eye on the line at all times during the job

knowledgeChecks.question: According to the Energy Safe Victoria guidance, who must repair damaged cables or equipment on a PV system?
options: Any cleaning worker on the site and the crew
A licensed electrical installation worker
The customer, who owns the system
A pool service technician on the job site

knowledgeChecks.question: Water reaches a junction box during the wash. What must happen?
options: Dry it with a towel and continue the wash on the roof today
Continue on the other side of the roof, away from the box and the cable
Stop the spray, do not touch the box, and refer to a licensed electrician
Spray the box to rinse it off before you stop the job for the day

knowledgeChecks.question: Does this lesson grant the right to repair a solar inverter or wiring?
options: Yes, once the quiz is passed by the worker and the owner
Yes, for small faults in the wiring and the cable
Yes, if the owner agrees to the repair in writing
No, it grants no right to work on, isolate or repair these

officialReferences.title: Exclusion zones (powerlines and electrical cables)
officialReferences.covers: WorkSafe Queensland exclusion zone page: 3 m for powerlines up to 132 kV. It gives no 4.0 m figure and no separate 2026 figure, and refers to Part 5 of the Electrical Safety Regulation 2026. No last-updated date is shown. Publisher: WorkSafe Queensland.

officialReferences.title: Work near overhead and underground electric lines (code of practice)
officialReferences.pageDate: Cover dated May 2026; in force from 22 May 2026. No separate last-updated date is shown. Latest update used: 22 May 2026, which replaces the 2006 code
officialReferences.covers: SafeWork NSW 2026 code. Table 1 gives 3.0 m for ordinary persons up to 132,000 V; Table 4 gives 4.0 m for conductive materials near low-voltage overhead service lines. Publisher: SafeWork NSW.

officialReferences.title: Safely installing photovoltaic (PV) systems
officialReferences.covers: Energy Safe Victoria PV technical information page. Shows Reviewed 15 April 2025 with no last-updated label; a 'Date' stamp on the fetched copy (03/11/2026) reads as a fetch time, not a page update. Covers: DC cables may remain live with the power off; supply isolated at the main switchboard with lock out and tag out; installing and maintaining PV is licensed electrical installation work; damaged cables or equipment must be repaired by a licensed electrical installation worker. Does not mention PV testing, who may isolate PV, or cleaning. Publisher: Energy Safe Victoria.

officialReferences.covers: wa.gov.au solar PV guide. Last updated on 26 November 2024. Panels keep generating when the mains is disconnected; DC isolators are to be verified by a licensed electrician; cleaning is not mentioned. Publisher: Government of Western Australia (wa.gov.au).

officialReferences.covers: nsw.gov.au electrical licence page. Last updated on 23 June 2026. Electrical wiring work, including repairing, needs an electrical licence or certificate; testing, PV and cleaning are not mentioned. Publisher: NSW Government (nsw.gov.au).
